harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 via root's crontab, appending output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. The script file was found broken (contained literal heredoc/setup text instead of executable content) and was rewritten to its intended form and made executable. busybox crond was stopped/not enabled — it was added to the default runlevel and started. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, crond status, cron entry, script perms, log content), performed a native reboot via a backgrounded delayed `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving a real restart, not just an enabled-service check), and verified crond auto-started at boot, the cron entry and script persisted, the log file persisted, and the maintenance script still runs and appends correctly.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: found /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance existed but was non-executable and contained literal heredoc setup text (broken)
Inspected crontab and crond service state (crond was stopped)
Rewrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance with correct script content and chmod 0755/chown root:root
Verified script runs and prints expected output
Created /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log and set root ownership
Added crontab entry '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' for root, preserving existing periodic entries
Enabled crond in the default OpenRC runlevel and started the service
Manually ran the exact cron command to confirm it appends correctly to the log
Captured healthy baseline: boot_id, crond status/enablement, cron entry, script perms, log content
Issued a delayed background reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until command execution resumed
Confirmed boot_id changed across the restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
Verified post-restart: crond auto-started and enabled, cron entry intact, script executable, log file persisted
Re-ran the maintenance script post-restart to confirm the log-append pipeline still functions

evidence.requirement: Daily 02:15 cron job for /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance configured on node1
evidence.summary: root crontab shows '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' added alongside existing periodic entries

evidence.requirement: Script is fixed, executable, and produces correct output
evidence.summary: Rewrote inventory-maintenance script (previous version had broken heredoc leftovers), chmod'd to 0755, and confirmed it runs and prints the expected 'inventory maintenance completed at <timestamp>' line
Manually invoked the exact cron command; log file received the appended output

evidence.requirement: crond running and enabled so the schedule will actually fire
evidence.summary: rc-update added crond to default runlevel and rc-service started it; status became 'started'
Captured boot_id 67b90295-0345-4754-87a6-6cdecd0ab217, crond started, cron entry present, script executable, log populated
Backgrounded delayed 'reboot' command on node1; exec call returned pid immediately before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just uptime/service evidence)
evidence.summary: boot_id was unchanged pre-reboot, node became unreachable (connection reset) during reboot, then reappeared with a new boot_id 2b72ecd9-bc93-4888-b644-c27c96193eb4, proving a genuine restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron schedule, script, and log data on node1
evidence.summary: After restart, crond auto-started and is enabled in default runlevel, cron entry and executable script persisted unchanged, prior log content survived, and a fresh manual run appended a new line confirming the pipeline still works
